CommandTrigger.description: Matches on the executable name of the command.
CommandTrigger.title: CommandTrigger

name.description: One executable name, or a list of names any one of which matches. Compared against the executable name only, never the whole command line. Every command in a pipeline is examined, and both the invoked path and its final component are compared.
name.title: Name

ignore_extension.description: Strip the file extension before comparing, so one entry `secretsdump` also matches `secretsdump.py`.
ignore_extension.title: Ignore Extension

CompositeTrigger.description:
Combines other triggers with AND or OR.

The YAML key is `trigger`, not `composite`: every other type is named after the thing
it inspects, and this one inspects other triggers. Writing `composite:` is an unknown
key, which is a hard validation error.
CompositeTrigger.title: CompositeTrigger

CompositeTriggerOptions.description: Options of a composite trigger (the `trigger` key).

operator.description: How the entries combine. AND requires every entry to match, OR requires one. Uppercase only.
operator.title: Operator

triggers.description: Names of triggers defined elsewhere, or inline anonymous triggers written in place — including a nested composite. An inline trigger has no name and cannot be referenced from anywhere else.
triggers.title: Triggers

CompositeTriggerOptions.title: CompositeTriggerOptions

DumpEnvAction.description: Writes the environment of the matched command into the artifact directory.
DumpEnvAction.title: DumpEnvAction

filters.description: ALLOWLIST of variable NAMES, matched with case-sensitive globs (`AWS_*`, `*_TOKEN`) and never against values. Quote any pattern beginning with '*': unquoted it is a YAML alias node, not a string. Absent or empty, this action captures EVERY environment variable in the command's environment, exported credentials and session tokens included.
filters.title: Filters

DumpKerberosAction.description:
Copies the Kerberos credential cache the matched command used.

Takes no parameters, but the empty mapping is mandatory: write `dump_kerberos: {}`. A
bare `dump_kerberos:` is YAML null, which fails validation and drops the whole source.

The cache comes from `KRB5CCNAME` in the command's environment; when that is unset,
`/tmp` is scanned for `krb5cc_<digits>` instead.
DumpKerberosAction.title: DumpKerberosAction

DumpKerberosOptions.description: Options of a `dump_kerberos` action: it takes none.
DumpKerberosOptions.title: DumpKerberosOptions

EnvVarTrigger.description: Matches when a given environment variable is set for the command.
EnvVarTrigger.title: EnvVarTrigger

variable.description: One environment-variable name, or a list any one of which matches. This is a PRESENCE test: the value is never compared and an empty value still counts as set. No globbing on the name.
variable.title: Variable

ExecCommandAction.description:
Runs a shell command on the operator's behalf and stores its output.

This is remote code execution by design: the command runs inside the container every
time its rule fires, unfiltered and unconfined. Trusting a profile source is trusting
it to run code in your container.
ExecCommandAction.title: ExecCommandAction

command.description: Shell command executed inside the container after the matched command finishes, in the operator's own zsh with `~/.zshrc` sourced, so aliases and shell functions resolve as they do at the prompt. It is not filtered and not confined.
command.title: Command

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before the command's whole process group is killed and the artifact records that it was cut short. Omit it, or write 0, for no limit. Negative values are refused.
timeout.title: Timeout

anyOf.description: A byte count (1048576) or a size string with a binary-unit suffix (100MB, 512KB, 2GB). K/M/G/T are powers of 1024.

max_output.description: Output cap applied to standard output and standard error SEPARATELY. Beyond it, output is dropped and the artifact is flagged as truncated. Omit it for the 1 MB default, or write 0 to keep everything. Negative values are refused.
max_output.title: Max Output

LogOutputConfig.description:
Inline terminal-output capture, overriding `sentinel.log_output` from `~/.exegol/config.yml`.

These three keys are the whole block, and a profile block replaces the machine default
WHOLESALE rather than being merged key by key. Note that `enabled` is settable here and
in `~/.exegol/config.yml` only — a CONTAINER profile can never supply it.

enabled.description: Embed the command's terminal output in every audit event. On by default: the event field is the primary destination, the `output_capture` artifact action being opt-in.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_size.description: Cap on the CLEANED UTF-8 text embedded in the event, cut on a character boundary. Defaults to 4KB, which keeps the output plus the event metadata under the 10000-byte default a stock Splunk truncates at. Must be strictly positive: this is the ONE knob here where 0 does not mean unlimited, because the field rides on EVERY event — switch the field off with `enabled: false`, and use an `output_capture` action to keep a whole window.
max_size.title: Max Size

truncation.description: Which end of an oversized capture to keep. `both` spends half the budget on each end and names the dropped byte count in between.
truncation.title: Truncation

LogOutputConfig.title: LogOutputConfig

LogRotationConfig.description:
Rotation of the event stream, overriding `sentinel.log_rotation` from `~/.exegol/config.yml`.

These four keys are the whole block. The interval that debounces two consecutive
rotations is fixed product behaviour, not a tunable: declaring a fifth key fails
validation and drops the whole source.

enabled.description: Turn rotation of the event stream on or off.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_size.description: Rotate once the event stream grows past this. Defaults to 100MB. 0 means NEVER rotate, matching `max_files` below — and rotation is the only bound on the event stream, so at 0 it grows until the disk does. Negative values are refused.
max_size.title: Max Size

max_files.description: How many rotated generations to keep. 0 keeps all of them; nothing is ever deleted.
max_files.title: Max Files

LogRotationConfig.title: LogRotationConfig

NetworkCaptureAction.description: Runs a packet capture spanning the matched command's execution.
NetworkCaptureAction.title: NetworkCaptureAction

interface.description: Interface passed straight to `tcpdump -i`. `any` captures on every interface at once.
interface.title: Interface

duration.description: Fixed capture window in seconds. Omit it to capture for as long as the matching command runs.
duration.title: Duration

OutputCaptureOptions.description: Options of an `output_capture` action: a command's terminal output kept as an artifact.

format.description: Which bytes land on disk. `raw` is the pty stream verbatim — replayable, with colours and control sequences kept. `text` is the same cleaning the inline event field applies. There is no combined value: capturing one command both ways is two actions on the rule, each with its own file pair and manifest.
format.title: Format

anyOf.description: A byte count (1048576) or a size string with a binary-unit suffix (100MB, 512KB, 2GB). K/M/G/T are powers of 1024.

max_size.description: Cap on the captured payload. Omit it, or write 0, for UNLIMITED — the author targeted this command and wants all of it. To keep nothing, do not declare the action at all. Negative values are refused.
max_size.title: Max Size

truncation.description: Which end of an over-cap capture survives. Only meaningful alongside `max_size`: declaring it without one is refused, because a truncation mode that can never fire is a setting the operator believes is protecting them.
truncation.title: Truncation

OutputCaptureOptions.title: OutputCaptureOptions

ParameterTrigger.description: Matches when a given argument is present on the command line.
ParameterTrigger.title: ParameterTrigger

argument.description: A single argument, matched exactly against the command's parsed arguments. Values are never inspected, so `-k` matches that flag wherever it appears. When the argument is not a standalone token, a plain substring test against the command as typed is used as a fallback.
argument.title: Argument

Profile.description:
A named audit profile: a list of rules, and optional per-profile settings.

An unknown EXTRA key at this level is silently ignored, so a stray `confg:` beside a
valid `rules:` loads a healthy-looking profile that collects nothing. When a profile
validates but never fires, re-read its own keys first.

rules.description: Rules, evaluated independently against every command.
rules.title: Rules

Profile.title: Profile

ProfileConfig.description: Optional per-profile settings, alongside `rules:`. Exactly three keys.

log_output.description: Inline terminal-output capture for this profile. Omitted, the machine default from `sentinel.log_output` in `~/.exegol/config.yml` is backfilled host-side, exactly as `log_rotation` is; a block here replaces that default WHOLESALE rather than being merged key by key.

env_redact.description: DENYLIST of environment-variable NAMES whose VALUES are masked to the literal `<REDACTED>` wherever they would be logged — the dump_env artifact and the captured environment of the command alike. Matching is case-sensitive and the whole name must match, so `KRBTGT*` covers `KRBTGT_SECRET` but a bare `TOKEN` covers only the variable named exactly `TOKEN`. Quote any pattern beginning with '*'. There is no default: a profile that omits it redacts NOTHING. Distinct from dump_env's `filters`, which is an allowlist deciding what is collected at all.
env_redact.title: Env Redact

ProfileConfig.title: ProfileConfig

ProfileRule.description:
One rule: run these actions when these triggers match.

Rules are evaluated independently against every command, so adding one never changes
what an existing one collects. Both keys are REQUIRED — misspelling either (`action:`
for `actions:`) is a missing-required-field error that drops the whole source.

triggers.description: A plain list of trigger names (combined with AND), or the long form with an explicit `operator` and `refs`.
triggers.title: Triggers

actions.description: Action names to run when the triggers match. Same resolution rule as triggers: own source first, then `core`.
actions.title: Actions

ProfileRule.title: ProfileRule

ProfileRuleTriggers.description: The long form of a rule's `triggers`, and the only way to get an OR at rule level.

operator.description: How the referenced triggers combine. Uppercase only.
operator.title: Operator

refs.description: Trigger names. A bare name resolves in this profile's own source first, then falls back to the official `core` source; an explicit `sourcekey.name` forces that source and never searches elsewhere.
refs.title: Refs

ProfileRuleTriggers.title: ProfileRuleTriggers

RegexTrigger.description: Matches a regular expression anywhere in the command line.
RegexTrigger.title: RegexTrigger

pattern.description: Python regular expression, SEARCHED against the command line rather than anchored to it — no `.*` padding is needed at either end. Quote it in YAML: a bare pattern containing ':', '#' or a leading '*' is not the string it looks like. Both the command as typed and its alias-resolved, variable-expanded spelling are tested, and a match on either one fires.
pattern.title: Pattern

ignore_case.description: Apply the case-insensitive flag to the search.
ignore_case.title: Ignore Case

description:
A Sentinel profile file: the triggers, actions and profiles one source declares.

Each of the three blocks maps a NAME to a definition. Names may contain letters,
digits, '_' and '-' only, because '.' is the source separator in a `sourcekey.name`
reference.

One invalid file takes its ENTIRE source namespace down with it: every profile,
trigger and action declared by that source disappears and `-S` reports the profile as
not found, even though the file is visible on disk.

triggers.description: Named conditions. The single key under a trigger's name IS its type: `command`, `regex`, `parameter`, `env_var`, or `trigger` for a composite.
triggers.title: Triggers

actions.description: Named collectors. The single key under an action's name IS its type: `dump_env`, `network_capture`, `dump_kerberos`, or `exec_command`.
actions.title: Actions

profiles.description: Named profiles, each selectable with `exegol start -S <name>`.
profiles.title: Profiles

title: SentinelConfig
